s: A company is migrating a large on-prem Oracle database (with stored procedures) to AWS. The solution must use managed services, be highly available, and enable afast migration with minimal downtime.
o: Use AWS DMS to replicate data to RDS for Oracle. Store database files in S3.
Use backup and restore into EC2-hosted Oracle cluster.
Use DMS to move data to DynamoDB. Recreate stored procedures in Lambda.
Use DMS to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Use AWS SCTto convert stored procedures.
e: Dis correct:Aurora PostgreSQLis afully managed, high-availability database engine. Use AWS DMSto migrate data and AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)to convert stored procedures from Oracle to Aurora-compatible code. This meets the requirements of minimal downtime,managed services, and stored procedure support. Ais not valid—RDS doesn't allow custom S3 integration for storage. Binvolves EC2, which violates the "managed services"constraint. Crequires complete rewrite of the application logic, which contradicts the minimal downtime requirement. Reference:https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.Aurora.html https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/Welcome.html

w.y: "Managed services", "highly available" and the stored procedures decide it per the key. AWS SCT converts the Oracle schema and stored procedures to Aurora PostgreSQL, and DMS with CDC moves the data with minimal downtime onto a managed, multi-AZ engine.

o.A: DMS to RDS for Oracle keeps the same engine, but DMS does not move stored procedures and storing database files in S3 makes no sense.
o.B: Oracle on EC2 is not a managed service and backup/restore means long downtime.
o.C: DynamoDB is not relational, and rewriting procedures in Lambda is a major rebuild.
o.D: Correct per key: SCT converts stored procedures and DMS migrates data to managed Aurora PostgreSQL.

alt: A homogeneous move to RDS for Oracle (Multi-AZ) is usually faster and needs no code conversion, so some pick A; its 'store database files in S3' wording is what makes D the safer exam answer.
